\section{Claim register}\label{sec:claims}
\subsection{Right-ideal semantics}\hypertarget{claim:semantics}{}\backmap
\textbf{LEAN.} Literal ordered membership and relation-respecting quotient right-action operation in the original ring. RightIdealBridge connects the displayed two-generator semiring carrier to a RingRightIdeal under explicit negation closure and proves quotient action laws; SupportDimension proves zero-quotient/membership equivalence and consumes explicit bottom-dimension/support/zero equivalences. OriginalCentralSupport gives the actual original-ring quotient and central-support zero bridge. CharacteristicSupport constructs a finite associated-layer support proxy from actual quotient classes, while SpecCharacteristicSupport identifies the genuine Module.support over a supplied commutative associated module and states its annihilator zero-locus boundary. ActualClassSupport connects a genuine filtered-layer quotient to that support boundary and records the WithBot/integer-defect correspondence under explicit class-map data. M01StructuralBoundary and the sequence-ring label obstruction show that the historical proposition-only class scaffold does not imply structural filtered-algebra facts; M01AssociatedGradedBoundary shows generic filtration data need not have commutative associated layers, and CentralFieldFiltrationBoundary exposes an incompatible degree-zero field-image requirement. CharacteristicSupportProducer consumes explicit per-prime ambient producers and localized common-quotient zero bridges to prove a genuine module-support inclusion. The full filtered-class/Spec(gr U) construction remains open. TerminalBoundary extracts literal original-U cofactors from a supplied zero quotient or membership witness, while Package/Opposite transports left S1 to right S1 in the opposite ring and conversely.

\subsection{Scalar-pencil utility}\hypertarget{claim:scalar}{}\backmap
\textbf{LEAN.} Finite exceptional scalars and simultaneous forbidden-set avoidance for finite division-ring coordinates and central-field matrix blocks with nonzero starting coordinates. PencilBridge, ActivatedPencil, MatrixPencil, DivisionLLD and RadicalLift conditionally infer top-to-cyclic, finite affine-source or finite top-lifting consequences from supplied data. FiniteOrbitPencil derives finite exceptions from an actual finite orbit basis over a commutative scalar extension while preserving the ordered activated identity; DerivedOrbitPencil constructs that orbit basis under an explicit finite central-dimension hypothesis. JacobsonScalarExtension packages the same top comparison through the actual Jacobson quotient while retaining the scalar-extension orbit basis, ExplicitBlocks consumes explicit finite composition, division-ring or repeated matrix block data, IsotypicBlocks exposes the remaining noncommutative repeated-block finite-bad-set theorem, and DivisionEigenBoundary isolates that witness family as an explicit hypothesis. WeightedDetectionComposition composes finite triangular detection with a nilpotent right correction. The scalar-extension theorem still requires the finite orbit basis and top comparison, and does not handle noncommutative endomorphism division rings. Repeated simple factors beyond the explicit block consumer, radical construction and the arbitrary finite-length activation theorem remain open M06–M07 work.

OriginalTestContract records the M06 original-U finite-test/source witness shape; DivisionLLD and DivisionLLDList add concrete finite affine source-avoidance families with arbitrary offsets and nonzero tails, with the list-indexed interface preserving one multiplier for every test and removing source-zero scalars; OriginalDivisionProducer constructs one literal nonzero original-U affine source from a certified finite list carrying explicit division-coefficient pencil bridges, and its ActualOriginalDivisionTest bridge derives that source from genuine finite division-ring top data and cyclicity equivalences. \subsection{Strong P\_h contracts}\hypertarget{claim:ph-scaffold}{}\backmap
\textbf{LEAN-SCAFFOLD.} Record affine source membership, abstract finite generation tests, integer defect bounds, both lower-index calls and supplied successor output. TestRetention makes carried lists, old/new component bookkeeping and defect arithmetic explicit; SupportRemovalArithmetic derives the successor defect bound from strict support removal; ConcreteSuccessor makes the old/new families and carried-list obligations Fin-indexed; ConstructiveSuccessor derives a successor witness from explicit base/two-call construction data and composes constructive base/successor rules to P\_(D+1); TwoCallAffineProducer removes the pre-built affine-source and output witness fields by deriving the pencil coefficient and assembling the next witness from the two lower calls plus explicit support/test implications; TwoCallDescentProducer packages the same two-call successor with an explicit finite exceptional set, support-defect equality, and carried-test conclusions; FiniteRemovalRetentionBridge consumes indexed strict-removal and test-retention hypotheses after one finite scalar choice; LayerSupportObstruction gives a concrete actual-support example showing why source-independent strict removal is invalid; FiniteScalarAvoidance proves finite unions of bad scalar sets can be avoided and supplies the finite-set arithmetic used by the two-call interface; SuccessorObstruction gives kernel-checked flat-defect and base-failure counterexamples showing that lower contracts alone cannot imply the required starting or successor decreases; FiniteIndex composes supplied P\_1 and successor rules, including D=0. \subsection{Finite-length boundary}\hypertarget{claim:length-scaffold}{}\backmap
\textbf{LEAN-SCAFFOLD.} MinimalPrimeLength wraps composition-series and finite-length closure facts and, given a supplied local model with Noetherian and Artinian hypotheses at a minimal support point, derives finite length and finite generation. MinimalPrimeLocalTheorem supplies a commutative local Noetherian theorem deriving finite length from a finite module whose maximal ideal is minimal over its actual annihilator. FilteredMinimalPrimeBridge derives the minimal-annihilator condition and finite length over an actual `Localization.AtPrime p` from support dimension zero. RightFiltration supplies an explicit finite right-module composition filtration with maximal adjacent inclusions and quotient data; ActualRadicalTop extracts finite generation, finite length, and Jacobson-quotient cyclicity from such a genuine filtration; GoodLocalBridge derives local finite generation, Noetherianity and finite length from explicit surjective and Artinian inputs. JacobsonTop proves actual radical-quotient generation reflection for finitely generated right modules, ActivatedFiniteLength consumes that criterion for an arbitrary finite family of supplied top blocks while retaining the ordered pencil identity, JacobsonScalarExtension packages the same top comparison through an actual Jacobson quotient and a supplied commutative scalar-extension orbit basis, and ExplicitBlocks consumes explicit finite composition/division-ring/matrix block data. These modules construct no characteristic support, localization or full minimal-prime bridge for the noncommutative paper module.

\emph{Source:} SymplecticStafford/FiniteLength/MinimalPrimeLength.lean; SymplecticStafford/FiniteLength/MinimalPrimeLocalTheorem.lean; SymplecticStafford/FiniteLength/FilteredMinimalPrimeBridge.lean; SymplecticStafford/FiniteLength/RightFiltration.lean; SymplecticStafford/FiniteLength/ActualRadicalTop.lean; SymplecticStafford/FiniteLength/GoodLocalBridge.lean; SymplecticStafford/FiniteLength/JacobsonTop.lean; SymplecticStafford/FiniteLength/ActivatedFiniteLength.lean; SymplecticStafford/FiniteLength/JacobsonScalarExtension.lean; SymplecticStafford/FiniteLength/ExplicitBlocks.lean.
\emph{Review:} Conditional checkpoint: local support point, surjective model, Noetherianity and Artinianity are supplied; M05 construction remains open.
